answerNotes.APPLE: An apple has a peel, flesh, and a seed-bearing core. Cider is made by pressing apples for their juice.
answerNotes.PEACH: A peach has a fuzzy skin and a hard pit. A nectarine is a close relative with smooth skin.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.SCALE: A scale measures weight. Its reading is different from a price, although a shop may calculate price using that weight.
answerNotes.PRICE: Price is the amount asked for an item. Change is money returned after a customer pays more than that amount.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.CASH: Cash means physical money such as bills and coins. A check gives an instruction to transfer money rather than being cash itself.
answerNotes.SIGN: Sign can be a public notice or the action of writing a name. Check whether the clue describes an object or asks for a verb.
answerNotes.TENT: A tent is a portable shelter made from fabric and supports. Its poles hold the shape while pegs or other anchors secure it.

answerNotes.CLOCK: A clock shows time. The hour hand moves more slowly than the minute hand on a traditional clock face.
answerNotes.BENCH: A bench normally seats more than one person. It can be used in a park, entryway, or bus shelter without changing that basic meaning.
answerNotes.HOUR: An hour contains sixty minutes. A minute contains sixty seconds; these two relationships are easy to mix up.
answerNotes.HAND: Hand can name a body part or a clock pointer. A clock's minute hand makes a full turn each hour.
answerNotes.FACE: Face can name the front of a head or the marked surface of a clock. The surrounding objects identify the sense used in the clue.
answerNotes.NUMBER: A number can count an amount or identify something. A telephone number identifies a connection rather than measuring its size.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.BRICK: A brick is a rectangular building block. In The Wizard of Oz, the yellow road is made from these blocks.

Notice displayed for people to read

answerNotes.TOWN: A town is a community. Its square or town hall is only one place within the larger community.
answerNotes.HALL: Hall can mean an entrance passage or a large gathering room. A town hall is a public building, while a hallway is a passage.
answerNotes.FLAG: A flag can be a cloth symbol or a small signaling marker. A mailbox flag shows a postal signal rather than identifying a country.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.BRICK: A brick is a rectangular building block. In The Wizard of Oz, the yellow road is made from these blocks.
answerNotes.FLOWER: A flower is the blossom, rather than the whole plant. In everyday speech, the word can also describe a plant grown for its blooms.
answerNotes.SIGN: Sign can be a public notice or the action of writing a name. Check whether the clue describes an object or asks for a verb.
answerNotes.WINDOW: A window admits light through glass. A screen is a mesh barrier that can keep insects out when the glass is open.

answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.
answerNotes.PHOTO: Photo is short for photograph. A caption or name label can preserve information that the image alone does not supply.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame surrounds and supports an image or object. The glass, backing, and outer border are separate parts of a picture frame.
answerNotes.GLASS: Glass is usually transparent but can also be colored. A glass is a drinking vessel, while glass without an article can name the material.
answerNotes.LIST: A list records items in order. Checking off a purchased item is different from changing the price or quantity of it.

words: Structure that sends water into the air
To scatter water by striking or stepping into it

answerNotes.FOUNTAIN: A fountain moves water through a spray or stream. The basin catches the water; it is one part of the whole structure.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.BASIN: A basin is an open container or depression holding water. In a garden fixture, it is the broad bowl below the spray or drinking rim.
answerNotes.STONE: Stone is a piece of natural rock. A slab is a relatively flat piece, while gravel consists of many smaller pieces.
answerNotes.COIN: A coin is a metal piece of money. The value depends on the currency and period; Bible stories do not use modern U.S. coins.
answerNotes.POOL: Pool can name swimming water or a small area collected in a hollow. A tide pool remains among shore rocks as the sea level falls.
answerNotes.RIM: The rim is the edge around an opening. A flowerpot, glass, and bowl each have a rim, but not all rims are the same shape.
answerNotes.BENCH: A bench normally seats more than one person. It can be used in a park, entryway, or bus shelter without changing that basic meaning.
answerNotes.PUMP: A pump moves liquid. A faucet or tap controls the opening through which the liquid comes out.
answerNotes.PEBBLE: A pebble is a small stone. Moving water can round its edges over time, giving a brook pebble its smooth shape.
